document.title: Deck App input harness: press every Pad Button, switch Deck Apps
document.summary: A new smoke-labelled CTest harness presses every Pad Button on every section of each example Deck App and switches to the next, failing fast on a Deck App failure or a stuck JS thread; the macOS ctest steps now exclude by the `smoke` label.
document.why: The minesweeper Triangle hang fixed in #135 slipped through every perf PR because nothing pressed Triangle in a Deck App or switched Deck Apps afterwards, so a hang blocked for an hour instead of failing fast [brief](source:s1).

sources.label: Orchestrator brief · Oct 27
sources.gist: Add a committed functional regression check that presses every Pad Button in each example Deck App and switches Deck Apps, failing fast on a hang; run it in the Linux Docker smoke path.

sources.label: 444f2ce
sources.title: fix(sdk): a pad button handler that re-renders runs once per press
sources.gist: The bug this harness must catch.

lookFor: The brief's ownership list is `tests/`, CMake, and scripts, but the change adds `event_queue_is_empty` under `src/core/`; no source asks for it, the harness needs it to tell a stuck handler from a slow one without stealing events [brief](source:s1).

The brief suggests an `alarm()` watchdog for hangs; at head the Triangle hang is caught by the queue-drain wait in `press`, and the alarm only reports a `js_runtime_stop` or shutdown that never returns [brief](source:s1).

groups.title: event_queue_is_empty
groups.why: The harness needs to see whether the JS thread has taken a press without popping the event itself.
groups.summary: `event_queue_is_empty` reads `queue.count` under the queue mutex, next to `event_queue_pop`.
lookFor: Production code in a test PR: a read-only helper with no caller in the app; nothing in the shipped host changes.

groups.title: The harness and its CTest wiring
groups.why: This is the regression check the brief asks for [brief](source:s1); it reproduces the hang of [444f2ce](source:s2) when that fix is reverted.
groups.summary: `run_deck_app_input_test.sh` stages the examples into a build-dir data root and runs `deck_app_input_harness`, which CMake builds from `HOST_RUNTIME_SOURCES` and registers with the `smoke` label and a 300 s TIMEOUT.
lookFor: Subtle: `press` waits for the queue to drain after the release, so a handler stuck in `onPressStart` leaves the pressend queued and fails as "JS thread hung after <button>"; a handler stuck in `onPressEnd` is reported against the next button pressed.
`ROUNDS 12` matches the demo's 12 sections because each round ends L, R, R; adding a demo section without bumping it leaves the last section's face buttons unpressed.

groups.title: Select smoke tests by label
groups.why: The new harness opens a window, so it must run where smoke runs and stay out of the macOS ctest (ADR 0002).
groups.summary: `smoke-docker.sh test` builds both smoke harnesses and runs `ctest -L smoke`, while CI's macOS step and `agent-check.sh host` switch from `-E smoke_harness` to `-LE smoke`.

groups.title: Docs follow the label
groups.why: AGENTS.md, ADR 0002 and the smoke skill named `smoke_harness` as the excluded test, which became inaccurate.
groups.summary: The docs swap `smoke_harness` for the `smoke` label and describe the input harness; wording only.

commits.subject: test: press every Pad Button in each example Deck App and switch Deck Apps
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The minesweeper Triangle hang fixed in #135 slipped through because no
check pressed Triangle in a Deck App or switched Deck Apps afterwards.
deck_app_input_harness presses Circle, Triangle, Square, L, R on every
section of each installed example and switches to the next. After each
press it waits for the JS thread to take the queued events, so a handler
that never returns fails within seconds naming the Deck App and button;
a SIGALRM watchdog covers a stop or shutdown that never returns.

It opens a window, so it carries the smoke label: smoke-docker.sh test
runs ctest -L smoke, and the macOS ctest steps exclude -LE smoke.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
